liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Sugaree** (3 reviews): Reviewer ranks this Sugaree among the best they've heard; Keith hammers away throughout the show; Sugaree is the insane highlight of the second half, with Keith and Jerry battling it out [7][11][12]
- **The Promised Land** (1 review): Keith plays the keys hard in the opener, and Bertha showcases every band member; first-set pace is laidback but not sandbagging [10]
- **Peggy-O** (1 review): Peggy-O is described as beautiful, and Bertha as rocking [7]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): First Jack Straw in about two and a half years; the crowd was excited to hear it [15]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): Reviewer calls it the best of the tour so far; the balcony shook during its raging outro [11]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Reviewer rates this one of the strongest Estimateds of the tour [11]
- **Friend Of The Devil** (1 review): Reviewer singles out Jerry's guitar work and emotional playing in a song they call "Comes a Time" [17]
- Piano opens with a figure reminiscent of the Wharf Rat prelude; Garcia plays nice ascending scalar runs, though pace drags [6]

## The recordings

- **gd77-05-03.moore.minches.17954.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 24 songs; 192 min; rated 4.4/5 by 5 [1]. Said about its sound: Audience recording has badly distorted bass; turning bass down helps, and it suits headphone listening [7]
- **gd1977-05-03.aud.glassberg.motb.0042.86241.flac16**: audience recording; 24 songs; 193 min; rated 4.4/5 by 20 [3]. Said about its sound: The Glassberg audience recording is described as a nice-sounding source; Glassberg audience recording sounds excellent, with no flaws noticed by the listener; Moore source was chosen for patches because its pitch matched a tuned guitar's A, and it was recorded from the front balcony [3][15][16]
- **gd77-05-03.set1-sbd.miller.21646.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 68 min; rated 4/5 by 6 [5]. Said about its sound: Soundboard of the first set sounds somewhat muddy rather than crisp, with bass levels running a bit high; On the soundboard, Garcia's quick runs up and down the fretboard come through clearly, as do Donna, Jerry and Bob's vocals on slow songs [6][9]
- **gd1977-05-03.141831.sony.ecm33p.moore.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: audience recording; 24 songs; 190 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer recalls Phil, Jerry and Bob facing each other in a circle in earlier years, unlike later on-stage separation [13]
- Reviewer calls this the best second set of 1977 among shows they saw or heard that year [17]
- The three sources run at different speeds; the first-set-only soundboard runs faster than the Moore source [3]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd77-05-03.moore.minches.17954.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Jerry Moore from first row loge or orchestra row 6 or 8; transferred by David Minches; source: Audience Recording [1]. Also: Analog-to-digital transfer by David Minches; EAC by Rango Keeshevan; shn encoding by Matt Vernon [1]
- **gd1977-05-03.aud.glassberg.motb.0042.86241.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and D. McCabe; source: udience 1st Row Loge Sony ECM XXX > Sony TCD5 X> MAC Mics spaced 30ft. [3]. Also: The Glassberg master cassettes run slow, about 2.6% slower than the Moore source, and had not circulated before [3]
- **gd77-05-03.set1-sbd.miller.21646.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1977-05-03.141831.sony.ecm33p.moore.dalton.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Jerry Moore and Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Jerry Moore's Master Audience Cassettes; Sony ECM-33P mics > Sony TC-158SD (Maxell UD-XLII with dolby B) > PCM [2]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by RareVinyl.com: [Grateful Dead Dave's Picks, Volume 50 (The Palladium, New York, NY - 5/3/77) 2024 US 4-CD set](https://us.rarevinyl.com/products/grateful-dead-dave-s-picks-volume-50-the-palladium-new-york-ny-5-3-77-us-4-cd-album-set-r2726104-866521) [19]
- Poster by Pete Mason: [Dave’s Picks Volume 50 features Spring 1977 Grateful Dead](https://nysmusic.com/2023/12/17/daves-picks-volume-50-features-spring-1977-grateful-dead/) [20]
- Fan art by thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com: [Grateful; Dead - Dave's Pick's #50 1977-04-04 The Palladium, New York City, NY](https://thecurtainwithblog.blogspot.com/2024/05/grateful-dead-daves-picks-50-1977-04-04.html) [21]
